quote: I just got a few questions to get started. Is that okay?
stewart_read: Intro named Ion and referenced the online form (partial legitimacy anchor), but rep rushed past any pause for rapport and straight into questions before customer had even settled.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as efficient rather than a gap, but the customer's immediate 'I'm driving' pushback suggests she wasn't given room to orient first.
coaching_implication: Slow the open by a beat — confirm she has a moment before diving into the qualifier list, especially once she flags she's driving.

quote: Okay. I'm driving right now. But go ahead and ask. Go ahead.
stewart_read: Customer flags a real constraint (driving) that affects both safety and her ability to focus; rep never acknowledges it or offers to call back at a better time.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged it low-risk since she kept answering, but driving-while-on-a-qualification-call is a legitimate safety/attention issue the schema would want addressed.
coaching_implication: Offer a callback option when a customer discloses they're driving, rather than plowing through the full script.

quote: But I think it needs it might need to be replaced.
stewart_read: Direct roof-replacement signal handed to the rep unprompted; the schema's bridge template (offer roofing team to look at it) was never deployed.
coaching_implication: This is exactly the trigger phrase the schema flags — rep should have asked follow-up questions and offered to route to the in-house roofing team, not just noted availability.

quote: That's fine. We have our own in house roofing.
stewart_read: Second touch on the same roof signal — rep states the fact of in-house roofing but doesn't route or offer it, immediately pivoting to the credit question instead.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be seen as sufficient acknowledgment, but schema explicitly calls for a bridge offer ('want me to have our roofing team take a look?'), which never happened.
coaching_implication: Close the loop: ask if she wants the roofing team to check it out and capture that as a separate lead thread, per the SESSION18_fcbf33c1 positive example.

quote: Oh, the power bill is about $1.50.
stewart_read: Bill figure captured (likely misheard/garbled, possibly $150) but rep responds with a flat acknowledgment and moves straight to the roof question — no reflection, no emotional flip.
coaching_implication: Reflect the bill number back ('that adds up over a year — that's exactly what we look at to see your savings') to plant the hook before moving on.

quote: That tree there, are you willing to remove it?
stewart_read: Rep runs a shading/tree-removal check efficiently and gets a quick yes, one of the few smoothly-handled beats in the call.
coaching_implication: No coaching needed here — good pace, clear question.

quote: But on your power bill, there's a yearly kilowatt usage history. We just need a picture of the graph it shows.
stewart_read: Call ends on logistics of a bill photo with zero appointment ever proposed — no date, no time, no 'is that fair' handshake, nothing.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be sequencing correctly (get bill, then set appointment in a follow-up call), but nothing in the transcript indicates a next-step commitment was made or even mentioned.
coaching_implication: Even without the bill in hand, the setter should propose a tentative appointment time contingent on the photo arriving, rather than ending with no next step owned.
